newsitem.title: CHINA: Delphi breaks ground on Shanghai battery plant.
newsitem.headline: Delphi breaks ground on Shanghai battery plant.

text.p: Delphi Energy & Engine Management Systems, a division of Delphi Automotive Systems, broke ground on Wednesday on its new $55 million joint venture battery production plant in Shanghai, a company official said.

The plant, in the Pudong development zone east of Shanghai's city centre, is 60 percent owned by Delphi and 40 percent by Shanghai Electrical (Group) Company, a state-owned conglomerate. Delphi Automotive is a unit of General Motors Corp.

Delphi Energy & Engine's general manager Don Runkle told a news conference the new facility, which is to begin production in early 1998, was the first plant in China to manufacture maintenance-free automotive batteries.
The target capacity is more than two million units annually, of which about 60 percent will be exported, depending on market conditions, Runkle said.
The original contract for the plant was signed in November 1995 and envisaged investment of US$29.9 million and production of one million batteries per year.
Michael Julius, general manager of the joint venture firm, said the expansion of the project had resulted from a reassessment of market potential by the partners.
Delphi's total investment in China, through its 10 joint ventures, now exceeds $200 million, company officials said.
